blocks.orig: A wildebeest is a type of antelope, and its population currently stands at 1.5 million as of 2020.
blocks.html: The wildebeest belongs to the antelope family, and as of 2020 its population numbers 1.5 million.

blocks.orig: These horned mammals are known for being surprisingly active and energetic, and they are actually incredibly fast.
blocks.html: These horned mammals have a reputation for being surprisingly lively and energetic, and in fact they are remarkably quick.

blocks.orig: This guide will tell you everything you need to know about the wildebeest and how fast they can really run. Do you want to see these incredible animals yourself, or do you want to experience The Great Migration? Have a look at our Tanzania Safari packages.
blocks.html: In this guide you will find everything worth knowing about the wildebeest and just how fast it can run. Would you like to see these remarkable animals with your own eyes, or witness The Great Migration? Take a look at our Tanzania Safari packages.

blocks.orig: The wildebeest’s proportions are off. The animal’s legs and back are slender, but its front end is heavy.
blocks.html: A wildebeest’s build is oddly out of balance: the animal’s legs and back are slim, yet the front end is heavy.

blocks.orig: The wildebeest has broad shoulders and a rectangular-shaped head. Its wide forequarters, which are padded with thick muscles, are complemented by a massive muzzle.
blocks.html: It has broad shoulders and a boxy, rectangular head. The wide forequarters, cushioned with thick muscle, go together with a huge muzzle.

blocks.orig: Others are more of a blue-gray color, while others have a light gray brush. Gray-brown wildebeests have the deepest coloring.
blocks.html: Some are more blue-grey in colour, others carry a light grey sheen. The deepest colouring belongs to the grey-brown wildebeest.

blocks.orig: Dark brown stripes running vertically across their bodies are visible on their shoulders.
blocks.html: On their shoulders you can make out dark brown stripes running vertically down the body.

blocks.orig: A thick, long, black mane is present on wildebeests. They have a long, either black or light, beard on their neck.
blocks.html: A dense, lengthy black mane runs along the wildebeest, and from its throat hangs a lengthy beard, which can be dark or pale.

blocks.orig: Wildebeests also have horns that curl away from their heads. The horns of a male wildebeest are twice as large as those of a female.
blocks.html: Their horns curve outwards, away from the head. A male's horns are twice the size of a female's.

blocks.orig: The horns of a male wildebeest are 84 cm (33 inches) long, while those of a female range in length from 30.5 to 40.5 cm (12 to 16 inches).
blocks.html: On a bull the horns reach 84 cm (33 inches); on a cow they measure anywhere between 30.5 and 40.5 cm (12 to 16 inches).

blocks.orig: Normally, the blue wildebeest reaches a height of 1.38 meters (4.5 feet). Additionally, they can weigh up to 272.2 kilograms (600 pounds).
blocks.html: The typical blue wildebeest stands 1.38 metres (4.5 feet) at the shoulder, and its weight can go as high as 272.2 kilograms (600 pounds).

blocks.orig: In grassy plains and woods, wildebeest live. Most of them reside in diverse regions of Eastern Africa.
blocks.html: Wildebeest make their home on grassy plains and in woodland. The majority of them are found across various parts of Eastern Africa.

blocks.orig: The wildebeest also reside close to the South African Orange River in the southern region of Africa.
blocks.html: In the south of the continent, wildebeest also live near the Orange River in South Africa.

blocks.orig: The Acacia savannas are where this animal chooses to spend most of its time.
blocks.html: The Acacia savannas are where this animal prefers to spend the bulk of its time.

blocks.orig: Due to the soil’s wetness, the grass grows swiftly and is excellent for finding plenty of grass to eat while grazing.
blocks.html: Because of the soil’s dampness, the grass shoots up quickly, which makes it an ideal spot to find plenty to eat while grazing.

blocks.orig: Although wildebeest often coexist with one another, they have also been observed sharing temporary residences with zebras they come across on the plains.
blocks.html: Wildebeest usually keep company with their own kind, but they have also been seen sharing temporary quarters with zebras they meet on the plains.

blocks.orig: This is so that wildebeest can reach the grass underneath, which is why zebras nibble away at the top layer of grass.
blocks.html: The zebras nibble off the top layer of grass, which in turn lets the wildebeest get at the grass beneath.

blocks.orig: Wildebeest are perpetual travelers because of their diet. They are continuously on the lookout for grass and water, which they consume twice daily.
blocks.html: Their diet turns wildebeest into permanent wanderers: they are forever searching for grass and water, which they take in twice a day.

blocks.orig: When it’s dry out, they graze on new grass before making their way back home before the rainy season starts.
blocks.html: When it’s dry, they feed on freshly sprouted grass and then make the journey home before the rains set in.

blocks.orig: They return to the area and resume grazing after the rainy season is over.
blocks.html: Once the rainy season has passed, they come back to the area and carry on grazing.

blocks.orig: The broad mouth of the wildebeest allows them to consume large amounts of grass quickly. When grass is scarce, they look for food in trees and shrubs.
blocks.html: Thanks to its wide mouth, a wildebeest can take in large quantities of grass in a short time. When grass runs short, it turns to trees and shrubs for food.

blocks.orig: A wildebeest’s vulnerability to its prey increases with size. A herd of wildebeest will assemble and start trampling the ground to defend itself.
blocks.html: A wildebeest’s exposure to its hunters grows with its size. In defence, a herd will gather together and begin stamping the ground.

blocks.orig: To let the herd know they are in danger, they also make loud noises to attract attention.
blocks.html: They also make loud calls to draw attention and warn the rest of the herd that danger is near.

blocks.orig: The fragmentation of the wildebeest’s habitat is another danger.
blocks.html: The breaking-up of the wildebeest’s habitat poses a further threat.

blocks.orig: World wildebeest populations are coming under more and more threat as agriculture and civilization advance and some regions’ water supplies continue to dry up.
blocks.html: As farming and human settlement expand, and certain regions’ water sources keep drying up, wildebeest populations around the world are coming under growing pressure.

blocks.orig: They are not in enough danger to be categorized as endangered, despite some of these difficulties.
blocks.html: In spite of these problems, they are not threatened enough to be classed as endangered.

blocks.orig: While wildebeest populations across the globe have been steadily declining, they have been growing in the Serengeti in recent years.
blocks.html: Although wildebeest numbers worldwide have been falling steadily, in the Serengeti they have actually increased in recent years.

blocks.orig: Only conservation efforts will be able to keep the wildebeest from going extinct.
blocks.html: Only conservation work can prevent the wildebeest from dying out.

blocks.orig: The blue wildebeest is a very wary creature and easily startled. This is due to the fact that they are prey for many apex predators across Africa, including cheetahs and lions.
blocks.html: The blue wildebeest is an extremely cautious animal that spooks easily. That is because so many of Africa's apex predators, cheetahs and lions among them, hunt it.

blocks.orig: When threatened, wildebeests can use their surprisingly incredible speed to escape capture by predators.
blocks.html: When danger looms, a wildebeest can call on its surprisingly impressive speed to avoid being caught by predators.

blocks.orig: A wildebeest can reach top speeds of 80 kilometers per hour, or 50 miles per hour.
blocks.html: At full tilt, a wildebeest can hit 80 kilometres per hour, or 50 miles per hour.

blocks.orig: As well as being extremely fast, they also have great endurance, which they use to migrate over long distances.
blocks.html: On top of its speed, it has great stamina, which it relies on to migrate across long distances.

blocks.orig: This is also a key trait when escaping predators like cheetahs. While a cheetah can outrun a wildebeest, it can only run quickly in short bursts. So, with a running start, a wildebeest is able to escape its grasp.
blocks.html: That stamina also matters when fleeing hunters such as cheetahs. A cheetah may be faster than a wildebeest, but it can only sprint in short bursts, so given a head start a wildebeest can slip out of its reach.

blocks.orig: Wildebeests are incredible creatures that are actually among the fastest land mammals in the world.
blocks.html: Wildebeest are remarkable animals and genuinely rank among the fastest land mammals on earth.

blocks.orig: Despite their thick, stocky appearance, they have amazing endurance and can reach high speeds when threatened by apex predators.
blocks.html: For all their thick, stocky build, they have tremendous endurance and can hit high speeds when apex predators threaten them.

blocks.orig: Their speed and endurance aid them tremendously during periods of migration and protect them against carnivores.
blocks.html: That combination of speed and stamina serves them enormously well during migration and keeps them safe from carnivores.
